title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 1st District
area: Western Massachusetts, including Springfield, Pittsfield, and the Berkshires

context.text: Incumbent Richard Neal defeated Jeromie Whalen, a Belchertown schoolteacher, in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary, 55.2% to 44.8%. No Republican candidate appeared on the primary ballot.

summary.text: Neal is the incumbent, serving since 2013 (and MA's 2nd District from 1989-2013). He is the Ranking Member of the House Ways and Means Committee and previously served as Mayor of Springfield and a Springfield city councilman.

background.text: Received a bachelor's degree from American International College (1972) and a master's degree from the University of Hartford (1976).
Worked as a staffer for Springfield Mayor William C. Sullivan, 1973-1978.
Served as a Springfield City Councilmember (1978-1984) and Mayor of Springfield (1984-1988) before election to Congress.

priorities.text: "I've fought tirelessly for policies that make a difference for hard-working families and future generations: fairer taxes, affordable and accessible healthcare, taking on climate change, preserving Social Security, and more."

Campaign statement: fighting "back against Donald Trump and Republicans' reckless budget that slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy and add trillions to the deficit."

positions.summary: Campaign describes fighting a Republican budget he says "slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy."
positions.quote: fighting back against Donald Trump and Republicans' reckless budget that slashes healthcare for working families to give tax breaks to the wealthy and add trillions to the deficit

positions.summary: Campaign material frames his record as pursuing "fairer taxes" and opposing tax breaks for the wealthy.
Cites "taking on climate change" among his record in Congress.

record.text: Serves as Ranking Member of the House Ways and Means Committee.
Statement on House passage of a War Powers Resolution following U.S. strikes in Iran, saying Congress "reminded the President and the nation who the power to declare war rests with."

candidates.name: Nadia Milleron

summary.text: Milleron is running as an unenrolled candidate. She holds a bachelor's degree from Smith College and a law degree from the University of Iowa, and has worked as an attorney and small business owner.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Smith College (1986) and a law degree from the University of Iowa (1994).
Career experience includes working as an attorney and small business owner.
